question.worked_solution:
To find ${f}^{-1}(x),$ we start by replacing $f(x)$ with $y:$

$$
y=\frac{1-x}{2x+3}
$$

Now, interchanging $x$ and $y$ gives

$$
x=\frac{1-y}{2y+3}.
$$

Then, we make $y$ the subject of the equation, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\frac{1-y}{2y+3} \\ x(2y+3) & =1-y \\ 2xy+3x & =1-y \\ 2xy+y & =1-3x \\ y(2x+1) & =1-3x \\ y & =\frac{1-3x}{2x+1}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the inverse function is 

$$
{f}^{-1}(x)=\frac{1-3x}{2x+1}.
$$
